Exposition devoted to Gramophone and radio sets

A cart, cart — an ancient type of transport designed for transporting goods and people, used in conjunction with a harness. A cart consists of such main parts as a shaft (ara–vashoti), a wheel (tegarchik) and an axle. A shaft consists of two 4.5 m long horse–drawn carriages (atliq), 8 pogona, two soloq and aygiz. Horse–drawn carriages are made of poplar. The shafts (70–80 cm in length) have one hole at each end to fasten the horse\'s neck.\n A wheel (tegarchik) consists of such parts as a gupchak, togyn, kegay, bellik, aravatemir, aravamikh and a pillow. Aravatemir and aravamikh are made of iron, and other parts are made of a type of resin (bujun) of kayragoch. The shaft is a piece of polished wood 40 cm thick and 2.5 m long, with both ends inserted into a round hole and a cart shaft mounted on it. A slat is placed under it to prevent the shaft from slipping while moving. Carts have two, three, and four wheels. Depending on the type of vehicle they are attached to, they are of different types, such as horse-drawn carts, camel carts, ox carts, and donkey carts.

Postal service is a system of institutions that receive and send letters, periodicals, parcels, money, etc. using means of transport. The emergence of postal service is directly related to the emergence of writing. In the Greek, Iranian, Egyptian, Chinese and Roman empires, postal service was of particular importance in state administration, and state postal service was well established: sent letters were transported on horseback and on foot on the principle of relays. With the development of crafts and trade, city post offices appeared that served artisans and merchants. At the same time, they also served other segments of the population.\nIn the 16th and 17th centuries, centralized royal post offices appeared in France, Sweden, England, and other countries. With the growth of postal communication and the development of interstate economic relations, postal communication also developed. The introduction of postal stamps into circulation marked a new era in the history of postal communication. In 1869, the postcard was introduced in Austria. In 1874, the 1st International Postal Congress was held with the participation of 22 countries, and an agreement was signed on the establishment of the Universal Postal Union (since 1878, the Universal Postal Union). In 1978, the Universal Postal Union Convention was adopted to coordinate correspondence and the exchange of written information around the world. The creation of steamships and locomotives at the beginning of the 19th century, and airplanes at the beginning of the 20th century, dramatically increased the speed of delivering mail. Postal services began to be used not only by the state, but also by ordinary citizens. The invention of the telegraph (1832), the telephone (1876), and the radio (1895) did not change the important place that postal communication held in the life of society. Even in the 20th century, it remained the most convenient and popular means of communication.

A television tower is a support on which the antennas of a television transmitting station are mounted. Sometimes the word "tower" is used, but it is slang and is no longer used in this sense.The zone of reliable reception of television and broadcasting signals depends on the height of the transmitting antennas on the television tower, so they are built as high as possible and placed at the highest points on the ground. The zone also depends on the power of the transmitters, so large television centers consume a large amount of electricity. The large capacity of the transmission cables (feeders), as well as their height and specific design, increase the likelihood of fires, which are very difficult to extinguish.

Money is a special commodity that acts as a general equivalent for all other commodities. Money plays a major role in the exchange of common commodities. In ancient times, various commodities served as money, such as cattle, hides, axes, etc. Later, precious metals served as money, because they did not lose their value and were very useful as a substitute for money. Money is not just a commodity, it has social value, that is, it serves as a means of purchasing all goods.

Gramophone (Greek gramma - letter, writing and phone - sound) - a device for reproducing sound recorded on a gramophone. In the groove of a rotating gramophone, the vibrations of the G. needle are transmitted to a membrane that is amplified by a speaker. A compact version of the G. is the phonograph. Since the 1950s, the electrophonium has been used instead of the G.

A radio receiver (abbreviated as receiver, colloquially as radio) is a device connected to an antenna and used for radio reception, that is, for the separation of signals from radio waves.A radio receiver is a radio receiver equipped with an antenna, as well as means for processing the received information and reproducing it in the desired form (visual, audio, printed text, etc.). In most cases, the antenna and the reproducing means are systematically part of the radio receiver. A radio receiver uses an antenna to spatially and polarize radio waves and convert them into electrical radio signals (voltage, current), change the frequency, separate the useful radio signal from the set of other (interfering) signals and noise that act at the output of the receiving antenna and do not coincide in frequency with the useful signal, amplify it, and convert the useful radio signal into a form that allows the use of the information contained in it. Officially, radio receivers are included in radio stations, although such a classification is rarely found in practice.
